selection_criteria: High discrimination (std > 1.0) with topic balance (2-3 per topic)

scenarios.text: Facing a $50M budget deficit, the city must choose: cut all library hours by 40% and close 2 of 8 branches, OR increase property taxes by 8%. Which approach do you support?

The city proposes a commercial rent tax (3.5% on businesses with revenue over $1M) to fund childcare and pre-K programs. Business groups warn this will push companies to relocate. Do you support this tax?

The city proposes opening a homeless navigation center (150 beds, services, no sobriety requirement) in a residential neighborhood. The site is 3 blocks from an elementary school. NIMBYs organize opposition. Do you support this location?

The city proposes a reparations program providing $50K direct payments to descendants of residents displaced by urban renewal (1950s-70s), funded by a 0.5% property transfer tax. Total cost: $200M over 10 years. Do you support this reparations program?

A developer proposes demolishing a 1920s historic theater (not formally landmarked) to build a 200-unit residential building. The theater has been vacant for 15 years; restoration would cost $25M with no clear tenant. Do you support demolition?

The city proposes offering Amazon a $50M tax break over 10 years to locate a fulfillment center creating 2,000 jobs (avg. wage $42K). Critics say this subsidizes low-wage work and harms local businesses. Do you support this deal?

The city proposes universal pre-K for all 4-year-olds, serving 2,500 children at a cost of $35M/year (funded by commercial property tax increase). Pre-K would be full-day, bilingual, and income-blind. Do you support this program?

Due to declining enrollment, the district must close 5 of 30 elementary schools or increase class sizes from 22 to 28 students district-wide. Closures would disproportionately affect lower-income neighborhoods. Which approach do you support?

The city proposes requiring all new buildings to be all-electric (no gas hookups) and existing buildings to convert by 2035. This would add $15K-$40K in retrofit costs for homeowners. Do you support this gas ban?

The city proposes a carbon fee on natural gas usage, starting at $20/ton ($12/month for average household) and increasing 5% annually. Revenue would fund climate adaptation projects in disadvantaged communities. Do you support this fee?

The city proposes participatory budgeting allowing residents to directly allocate $10M (5% of discretionary budget) through neighborhood assemblies and online voting. Staff warn this may slow down projects. Do you support this experiment?

A ballot measure would establish ranked-choice voting for all city elections, allowing voters to rank up to 5 candidates. This typically reduces negative campaigning and increases diversity of winners. Do you support ranked-choice voting?

The city is considering allowing fourplexes by-right on all single-family lots (similar to SB 9 but more permissive). Projections show this could add 2,000 units over 10 years but may change neighborhood character. Do you support this zoning change?

The city proposes expanding rent control to buildings constructed before 2010 (currently only pre-1995 buildings are covered), with annual increases capped at 3%. Landlord groups warn this will reduce rental housing investment. Do you support this expansion?

The police department wants to install 500 cameras with facial recognition at major intersections and transit hubs, costing $12M. Civil liberties groups oppose. Do you support this surveillance expansion?

The city proposes reallocating 25% of police budget ($40M) to create a new department of mental health crisis responders, homeless outreach, and violence prevention. Police staffing would drop from 800 to 600 officers. Do you support this reallocation?

A proposal would eliminate parking minimums for new development near BART stations (within 1/2 mile), allowing developers to build without any parking. Merchants worry about customer access. Do you support eliminating parking requirements?

The city plans to remove 200 parking spaces on a major arterial to add protected bike lanes, reducing car lanes from 4 to 2. Traffic modeling shows 15-minute delays during peak hours but expects 40% increase in cycling. Do you support this plan?

A developer proposes an 8-story, 120-unit apartment building on a surface parking lot downtown. 15% of units would be affordable (80% AMI). The project requires a zoning variance for height. Do you support this project?

The city council proposes requiring all new developments over 20 units to include 25% affordable housing (60% AMI) without any density bonuses. This would likely reduce market-rate housing construction by 30-40%. Do you support this policy?
